question: The audit trusts 463 of 1947 lifts, 24%. On the other 76% the engine declines to opine, so those harnesses can never produce a finding. WHY are they untrusted, and which cause is worth fixing?

two_hypotheses_that_were_WRONG.libc_and_local_noise: The top missed names are getpid, memcmp, read, __builtin_trap, _cleanup_, and harness-local helpers, which looked like the lifter penalising itself for calls it correctly ignores. Measured: only 9% of missed calls. 88% are GENUINE EXTERNAL CALLS.
two_hypotheses_that_were_WRONG.fuzzeddataprovider_plumbing: The dominant shape is member calls, and the first example was `stream.PickValueInArray(..)` -- harness plumbing rather than a library call. Measured across all receivers: `fdp` accounts for 60 of 2726. The rest are real library objects -- codec, db, parser, doc, options, phone_util.

THE_ANSWER: The gap is not a bug. It is a C lifter meeting C++ class-API harnesses. The untrusted verdict on those is CORRECT -- the engine cannot model `codec.decode(data, size)` and says so rather than guessing.
what_this_licenses: Building a member-call lift path is the single largest available increase in audit reach, and audit reach is what produced the one merged upstream fix. A receiver is a resource and a method is an op; the IR already expresses both.
what_it_does_NOT_license: Any expectation that 201 more trusted lifts yield 201 more findings. The current rate is 2 real defects in 463 trusted lifts. The honest projection is under one additional finding, and the case for doing it is compounding reach rather than a forecast.
